newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach expects light fines - paper.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach expects light fines - paper.

text.p: Stagecoach Plc may be fined less than 300,000 pounds ($481,700) ($481,700) over cuts in services on its South West Trains rail franchise caused by the company laying off too many drivers, the Times reported on Monday.

The paper quoted Stagecoach commercial director Peter Cotton as saying the company hoped to avoid the heavier fines of 600 pounds per train that regulator Opraf could levy, since most of the 39 cancelled services per day were not in peak times.
Instead Cotton expected penalties of less than 100 pounds per train, said the paper.
Last month South West Trains offered passengers a free day's travel after driver shortages caused widespread cancellations.
